uBO Lite (uBOL) is a reliable and efficient content blocker.

The default ruleset corresponds to uBlock Origin's default filterset:

- uBlock Origin's built-in filter lists
- EasyList
- EasyPrivacy
- Peter Lowe’s Ad and tracking server list

You can enable more rulesets by visiting the options page -- click the _Cogs_ icon in the popup panel.

uBOL is entirely declarative, meaning there is no need for a permanent uBOL process for the filtering to occur, and CSS/JS injection-based content filtering is performed reliably by the browser itself rather than by the extension. This means that uBOL itself does not consume CPU/memory resources while content blocking is ongoing -- uBOL's service worker process is required _only_ when you interact with the popup panel or the option pages.

When visiting a website, a person usually leaves a lot of information about himself. And without any measures on the part of the site owner, these personal data may be stolen. If you do not want something of the sort to happen, thing about accessing all sites via the HTTPS technology.

HTTPS Now is a Safari extension (content blocker) that protects your browsing activity by automatically enabling the HTTPS protocol on all websites that you visit. By loading the HTTPS version of websites into your browser, all your traffic will be encrypted, reliable and surveillance free.

Although major websites already encrypt the traffic by using HTTPS, it’s not guaranteed that you use this technology - sometimes is not active by default or some embedded assets are loaded through the default and unencrypted HTTP connections. Also, clicking links can redirect you to the insecure versions of sites. Actually more than 75% of websites out there still rely on unencrypted HTTP communications.

The HTTPS Now extension will fix these problems by rewriting all your requests from HTTP to HTTPS. It will also make sure that the assets from the visited websites (images, styles, scripts or ads) are transferred via the safe HTTPS and no one can steal your cookies, passwords, sessions or private data.

• What is the HTTPS protocol and why should you care?
Did you know that browsing the web in a coffee shop, airport or hotel with free internet access can be dangerous? Even your own home or company internet connection is not safe. This is because the common HTTP web traffic can be intercepted in clear text, inspected and even modified by anyone.
HTTPS has significantly more secure since this protocol will encrypt your communications.

• The benefits of the HTTPS protocol and why should you use it?
- Faster page loading: data sent over HTTPS loads faster since the new HTTP/2 protocol is available in Safari only on encrypted communications
- Confidentiality: no one can read your content, passwords or messages
- Integrity: your traffic cannot be modified - for example, no key-loggers can be injected
- Authentication: your site cannot be routed to a clone without you knowing it

• Is this a VPN service?
No, this extension is not a VPN service, but is very efficient and safe as a VPN. This extension will make sure you are using only HTTPS in your surfing and the usage of HTTPS will make your traffic encrypted, reliable and surveillance free. Also, HTTPS is much faster than a VPN.

Dark Mode is a Safari extension for iPhone and iPad. It turns light websites dark, so a white page doesn't light up the room when you read at night.

It's completely free: no ads, no in-app purchases, no subscriptions and no account.

Fixes for individual websites keep pages looking right, and they update by themselves: Dark Mode checks for new ones at most once a day.

ON, AUTO OR OFF
• On makes every website dark.
• Auto follows a schedule: your device's appearance, sunset to sunrise, or hours you choose.
• Off leaves websites as they are.
Sunset to sunrise is estimated from your time zone. If you allow location, it uses your location instead, rounded to about a kilometre.

THEMES
• Four presets: Default, Midnight, Warm and OLED (pure black).
• Sliders for brightness, contrast, sepia and grayscale.
• A preview in the app shows a page in your theme as you change it.
• Safari's Dark Mode menu adds more: dark or light scheme, Dynamic or Filter mode, background and text colors, selection and scrollbar colors, font, text stroke and dimmed images.

ONE WEBSITE AT A TIME
• Give a website its own theme.
• Exclude a website so it keeps its own colors.
• Websites that already have a dark theme are left as they are. You can use Dark Mode's theme on them instead.
• The Websites list in the app shows every site you've set up, so you can change or remove each one.

SETTINGS IN ONE PLACE
A change in the app shows in Safari's Dark Mode menu, and a change in Safari shows in the app. Turn on Sync with iCloud to use the same settings on your other devices signed in to your Apple Account. You can also export your settings to a file and import them later.

PRIVACY
To make a page dark, the extension reads it inside Safari, on your device. Nothing it reads leaves your device. Dark Mode has no accounts, no analytics and no ads.

GETTING STARTED
1. Open Settings › Apps › Safari › Extensions. On iOS 17, it's Settings › Safari › Extensions.
2. Turn on Dark Mode and allow it on all websites.
The Safari Setup Guide in the app shows each step.
